title: refactor: `BufferEncoder` registration for types and encoders
body:
**Summary**

This PR modifies `BufferEncoder` in two main ways:
 - Encoders and types aren't hard-coded in `BufferEncoder`. Types and their associated encoders are registered with the `BufferEncoder` class.
 - The lookup mechanism for encoders respects type hierarchy. This means that if you register an encoder for a subclass, then the encoder registered for its parent class will not be returned. This can happen with `isinstance` checks, the current method for encoder lookup.

This PR is in preparation for an update that allows `GoalState` objects to be serialized, a necessary feature for the Demonstrating Monty's Capabilities paper. For context, `GoalState` is a subclass of `State`, and they'll need different encoders to handle repackaging of their different attributes. This is the reason for the new lookup method.

Unit tests have also been added.
author: scottcanoe

comments.body: Tagging @vkakerbeck, @nielsleadholm, @hlee9212, and @ramyamounir for visibility since this came up in our research meeting.
Adding @jeremyshoemaker to also take a look.

title: Issue installing on ARM 64 MacOS 151.1
body:
### Describe the bug

Following the install instructions for Anaconda and Apple Silicon Mac mini M2 I see the following error with the 
```conda env create```
step. I am getting the following error dump

```(base) john@john-macmini tbp.monty % conda env create -f environment_arm64.yml  
Channels:
 - aihabitat
 - pytorch
 - pyg
 - defaults
 - conda-forge
Platform: osx-arm64
Collecting package metadata (repodata.json): done
Solving environment: failed

LibMambaUnsatisfiableError: Encountered problems while solving:
  - nothing provides requested aihabitat::habitat-sim =0.2.2*
  - nothing provides requested mkl <2022
  - nothing provides blas * mkl needed by pytorch-1.11.0.arm64-py3.8_0

Could not solve for environment specs
The following packages are incompatible
├─ habitat-sim 0.2.2*  does not exist (perhaps a typo or a missing channel);
├─ mkl <2022  does not exist (perhaps a typo or a missing channel);
└─ pytorch 1.11.0*  is not installable because it requires
   └─ blas * mkl, which does not exist (perhaps a missing channel).
```

I am running the following Python version
```(base) john@john-macmini tbp.monty % python --version
Python 3.12.7
```
author: doonhammer

comments.body:
Hi @doonhammer, I'm sorry that the install instructions are not working.

On Apple's ARM 64, the Anaconda instructions require to specify the environment file explicitly:
```
conda env create -f environment_arm64.yml
```
Is the above command the one that generated the error?

If you still get the same error even when specifying `-f environment_arm64.yml`, this may be a similar problem described in #81. There, the solution seemed to be to use the Miniconda setup instructions (if you're using `zsh` shell):
```
conda env create -f environment_arm64.yml --subdir=osx-64
conda init zsh
conda activate tbp.monty
conda config --env --set subdir osx-64
```
Or if you're using `bash` or some other shell:
```
conda env create -f environment_arm64.yml --subdir=osx-64
conda init
conda activate tbp.monty
conda config --env --set subdir osx-64
```
Adding --subdir=osx-64 did the trick with Anaconda install. Install succeeded and all tests passed. Thanks for the help

title: docs: avoid PRs based on unmerged PRs
body:
This Pull Request proposes to formalize that Pull Requests that depend on unmerged Pull Requests are invalid and should be avoided.

The main rationale is provided in the note:
> [!NOTE]
> Pull Requests that depend on unmerged Pull Requests add unnecessary complexity to the review process: **Maintainers** must track the status of multiple Pull Requests and re-review them if the dependent Pull Request is updated. Such dependency is much easier for the Pull Request author to track and to submit the Pull Request after all dependent code is already merged to `main`.

As this is a policy-related Pull Request, I am asking all Maintainers to review it.
author: tristanls

comments.body:
(Sorry for the above phantom review from another Github account I have... Will be more careful about making sure I'm logged in correctly)

I like this suggestion and think it will be useful. I also like Viviane's suggestion that it could be useful to enable draft PRs to depend on unmerged PRs. This enables more visibility of in progress code where relevant, without re-introducing the burden that your suggestion is fixing, which is the requirement to review a complex, multi-dependency PR.

Draft PRs are available in the repository, so they should be available for the use cases in y'all's comments.

I added:

> A Draft Pull Request is ignored and not triaged.

to the Pull Request Triage section.

title: ci: rightsize runners for specific jobs
body:
After rightsizing the runners, observed no significant changes in workflow runtimes. The test workflow runtime is uneffected because `pytest` was run with `-n 8`, so going from 16 to 8 cores had no apparent impact.

This reduces the cost of each Monty full-length workflow to less than a 1/3rd of current cost. From \~28min x $0.064 = **\~$1.792** to \~13min x $0.008 + 15min x $0.032 = $0.104 + $0.48 = **\~$0.584**

Why are we using paid 2-core instances instead of free-tier 2-core instances? free-tier 2-core instances do not have large enough disk to download and restore the cache after installing Monty \~5.7GB.
author: tristanls

comments.body:
The runtimes would not be affected if the jobs never used more than two cores and never needed much memory. Ruff checks are fast, so it doesn't make a difference. Other checks, aside from testing, are also quick, so multithreading doesn't help. Install might only be using a single core as well, so that could explain why it wasn't materially affected.

The split was because the minutes get charged different amounts in the new setup since they use different runners: $0.008/min (2-core) and $0.032/min (8-core), respectively.
okay, thanks for the explanation :) that makes sense

title: ci: explicit node size for ci jobs
body:
This Pull Request prepares the Monty workflow to use smaller GitHub-hosted runners to control costs per job by explicitly setting the runner label to the current `tbp.monty` default runners.

In the future, I will create smaller runners and follow up on Pull Requests using smaller runners (by changing the label) for jobs that don't need many cores to execute.
author: tristanls
